title: Integration Workshop — Sunridge Systems & Redwood
next_steps: Karen to share integration capability matrix and partner-deck by 2029-09-15
Jamal to run a short perf benchmark plan draft by 2029-09-20
Nadia and Redwood security team to schedule SOC2/ISO evidence review the week of 2029-09-23
action_items: Karen Liu: Send partner integration deck + architecture slides (due 2029-09-15)
Jamal Ortiz: Draft benchmark plan and sample test vectors (due 2029-09-20)
Nadia Chen / Redwood security contact: Exchange initial compliance questionnaire (due 2029-09-18)
Tom Bowers: Share current infra diagram and VPC peering constraints (due 2029-09-17)
summary: Introductory integration workshop to align on hybrid hosting partner model: routing, billing, security, and technical pilot scope. Sunridge is evaluating a reseller + managed GPU offering; priorities are predictable latency for inference, data residency and auditability, and control-plane separation.
questions: What are Redwood's SLAs for Dedicated pools?
Can we run inference in our VPC with customer KMS/HSM?
How does routing handle model fallback under capacity pressure?
transcript:
Header: 2029-09-13 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Karen Liu, Jamal Ortiz, Maya Patel (Redwood) — Priya Malhotra, Ethan Rios, Nadia Chen, Tom Bowers (Sunridge)

[00:00] Karen Liu: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Karen from Redwood, AE for the channel team. Quick round robin before we dive?
[00:07] Priya Malhotra: Hi — Priya here, we run cloud infra at Sunridge. Excited to talk partner model.
[00:11] Ethan Rios: Ethan — partnerships. We're exploring how we could resell or co-manage GPU capacity.
[00:15] Nadia Chen: Nadia, security architect — I'll focus on compliance needs.
[00:19] Tom Bowers: Tom, platform eng. I'll be doing the integration work.
[00:23] Jamal Ortiz: Jamal, SE at Redwood; I'll handle the tech deep stuff today.
[00:27] Maya Patel: Maya, solutions. I'll take notes and run through the quick demo after the arch discussion.

[00:40] Karen: High-level goal for this session: align on partner engagement (reseller vs OEM), technical constraints for private deployments, and an initial pilot scope for performance validation. We'll also surface security asks. Does that sound right?
[00:48] Priya: Yes, that's perfect. We're short on predictable latency for our enterprise customers; throughput matters but latency is the blocker.

[01:02] Jamal: Great. Quick architecture overview from Redwood — apologies if transcription's off, but we're talking: hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC deployments with a light control plane. Our runtime supports dynamic batching, kv cache (sometimes transcribed as "K V cashe") and model variants for fallback.
[01:21] Tom: Can you explain how the KV cache works across pooled and private modes? We worry about cold-starts and replication between availability zones.
[01:30] Jamal: Sure. The KV cache is per-inference session, we do prefix caching for repeated prompts; on Dedicated pools we can pin cache to a model shard so cold starts are reduced. In Private VPC, caching stays local and we offer an optional distributed cache layer if you want cross-AZ reuse — it needs a short design discussion about consistency and encryption.

[01:55] Nadia: Encryption — does Redwood let us bring our own KMS/HSM? That's a hard requirement for regulated customers.
[02:02] Karen: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments. We integrate with major KMS and enterprise HSM, but we'll need to map the exact rotation and key grant flow. We'll send the KMS integration doc.

[02:18] Ethan: On commercial model — we imagine a reseller arrangement where Sunridge packages Dedicated pools in our marketplace and we handle invoices. How does billing and metering work?
[02:29] Maya: Billing can break down to token usage for hosted, and committed capacity for Dedicated; for reseller we'd provide per-customer metering feeds and a billing reconciliation API. There's also a usage-export CSV and S3 hooks.

[02:52] Tom: Any friction with private control plane? We run strict network egress policies.
[02:58] Jamal: Private control plane minimizes egress, we can do control plane inside your VPC or an air-gapped variant. Might be some work to map audit logs and syslog streams to your SIEM.

[03:20] Priya: Performance — typical 8k-token models, many of our embeddings and real-time chat lanes are <512 tokens, but occasional bursts to 8k. What is the latency profile?
[03:31] Jamal: For typical 512-token SLOs, with Dedicated NVLink clusters you'd see p95 around 80–120 ms per token for some models; depends on quantization profile and sequence length. For 8k sequences overhead grows but we have kernel selections and KV cache to mitigate.

[03:53] Ethan: Are there fallbacks if a specific GPU type is busy? Like cheaper model variants?
[03:58] Jamal: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or to a lower-tier quantized instance. You can define policies: latency-first, cost-first, or region-priority.

[04:15] Nadia: Compliance evidence — SOC 2 and ISO? We need evidence for a procurement RFP.
[04:21] Karen: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and is ISO-pending for certain regions; we'll share the latest artifacts and an NDA-protected link. We'll also provide a list of control mappings for your auditors.

[04:33] Tom: Network: Do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalents to avoid public egress?
[04:37] Maya: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink patterns, and on-prem appliances for air-gapped setups. Some orchestration tweaks required for autoscaling.

[04:52] Priya: Pilot proposal — we'd like a 6-week pilot: provision a Dedicated pool in our EU region, run 3 customer flows (chat, rerank, embeddings), and validate p95 latency under our load. Also confirm BYOK and audit logging. Costs?
[05:05] Jamal: For a pilot, we usually do a small reserved block (example: 4 A100-equivalents) with metering for overage. We can prepare a cost estimate based on your expected qps.

[05:21] Ethan: Could Redwood provide a partner-discount for the pilot? Usually partners get a reduced trial rate.
[05:26] Karen: We'll propose a partner pilot pricing sheet. I'll include an example margin structure for reseller offers.

[05:34] [short crosstalk]

[05:45] Jamal: Quick demo note: I won't demo high-traffic now but I'll show routing and rollout in the console — small clip here.
[05:51] [08:10] Jamal: (demo) Console view — per-route dashboards, token usage, trace for a sample request. The rollout tab shows canary percentage and automatic rollback.
[08:28] Tom: That UI looks familiar but is there an API-first path? We need IaC support.
[08:33] Jamal: Yes, full API and Terraform provider. We version models and have rollout configs in code.

[09:05] Priya: Security follow-ups — will you accept our questionnaire? We have a 70-question RFP security doc.
[09:12] Karen: Yes, we'll complete it. For sensitive fields we can coordinate via your secure portal.

[09:23] Nadia: Data residency: some customers require that inference never leaves EU. For the pilot can you guarantee region pinning?
[09:30] Jamal: Region pinning is supported; routing policy can prevent cross-region fallback, though that impacts availability. We'll document tradeoffs.

[09:46] Ethan: Integration patterns — we want to embed Redwood endpoints into our marketplace onboarding flow and offer single-click provisioning. How much custom dev is typical?
[09:56] Maya: Usually a few webhooks and an API call to provision tenant-scoped Dedicated pools. We supply SDK snippets and a partner onboarding template.

[10:12] Tom: DevOps constraints: our clusters use Calico + strict egress; will you require inbound firewall changes?
[10:19] Jamal: For VPC peering, firewall rules are minimal, but you'll need outbound to some control-plane endpoints if using managed control plane. If air-gapped, we ship an on-prem package.

[10:33] [pause, background noise]

[10:46] Priya: What's the typical timeline from pilot sign to first traffic? 4–8 weeks?
[10:51] Karen: Typically 3–6 weeks: contract, infra provisioning, key exchange, and a short validation window. Air-gapped or heavy compliance can extend that.

[11:10] Ethan: On the competition, our SIs evaluated AICorp and VoltaCloud. What differentiates Redwood?
[11:17] Jamal: We're production-first: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, strong cost-controls (batching / kv caching / quant profiles), and built-in rollouts and observability — plus partner APIs for reseller flows.

[11:40] Tom: About KV cache again — what's the eviction policy if memory pressure occurs?
[11:45] Jamal: Eviction is LRU by default with pinning options per route. You can also configure TTLs for prefixes. We'll share config examples.

[12:06] Nadia: Audit logging — can we get token-level invocation logs but with PII scrubbed?
[12:12] Maya: Yes, we support redaction policies and can provide log streams to your SIEM. There's a default PII filter and you can add rules.

[12:28] Priya: Pilot success criteria — what should we measure? p95 latency under 95 percentile load, error rate <0.5%, and audit log completeness. That work?
[12:38] Karen: Sounds right. We'll align on exact test vectors.

[12:50] Ethan: What about model updates — do you support canary with label-based routing for different customers?
[12:57] Jamal: Yes, you can route by tenant ID and rollout models per-tenant or per-route with automatic canary analysis.

[13:12] Tom: Regarding orchestration: autoscaling — how do we avoid noisy neighbor issues?
[13:18] Jamal: Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated; we also offer isolation hints and admission controls to prevent co-tenancy impact.

[13:32] [16:00] Maya: Sharing links: partner-deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/partner-deck-sunridge) — Security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack-nadia) 

[16:20] Priya: We'll need an architectural diagram. Tom will share our current infra.

[16:32] Tom: I'll paste a high-level diagram to the chat after — nothing sensitive, but shows VPC topology.

[16:40] Jamal: For the benchmark plan: recommend 3 test vectors — short chat (<=128 tokens), medium conv (512 tokens), long-form (4k+). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and cold/warm starts. Also test fallback routing under simulated GPU exhaustion.

[16:59] Nadia: On the RFP: we'll need evidence of encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and clear key rotation docs.

[17:06] Karen: We'll attach KMS/HSM integration notes and rotation playbook.

[17:12] Ethan: Can Redwood do a co-branded press or marketplace listing?
[17:16] Karen: Yes, we have a channel marketing kit and listing process; we can share requirements.

[17:25] [minor interruption — someone joining late] 

[17:39] Maya: Quick recap from our side: we will deliver partner-deck, pilot pricing, and a benchmark plan. Security will get initial SOC2 artifacts.

[17:48] Priya: From Sunridge: Tom will send infra diagram and constraints, Nadia will send the security questionnaire, and Ethan will confirm partner commercial goals.

[18:00] Karen: Great. Any last questions?
[18:04] Tom: One more — if we want to bundle on-prem appliances for really sensitive customers, what's the typical install footprint?
[18:12] Jamal: On-prem appliance typically needs 4 x A100-equivalent nodes minimum for inference scale, plus a small control VM. We can provide an install checklist.

[18:25] Priya: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[18:28] Karen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the materials.
[18:30] [meeting ends]

Notes: Transcript contains natural disfluencies and occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K V cashe" for KV cache). References to links are represented as short URLs for shared docs.
